Residential and Business
Tract III comprises 14,745.92 acres and Tract II consists of 16,130.53 acres. There are currently a number of residential sites in the primary area of study. 17 residential structures are located within Tract III. Seven of these homes are inhabited while 10 have been abandoned. Most of the structures were built in the 1920's and 30's when the area was heavily settled. The smaller ranches were absorbed by the larger ranches during the past 40 years and as a result, many of the homes were vacated.
Within Tract II there are 9 residential structures of which 7 are inhabited and the remainder have been vacated.
The only business development in the area is the Spring Creek Bar and Cafe, which is on County Road 384 and serves the mine workers and local residents.
Crop Lands
Both tracts are similar to much of Eastern Montana, being primarily a sparsely settled range country devoted to the raising of livestock.

Most of the county is in native range with small islands of cultivation interspersed in the valleys and the smoother upland areas. Crops grown in the study area and the average yields for Big Horn County with approximate values per acre are shown in Table II-27.
